title: Famine Review Committee warns famine is imminent in northern Gaza
body:
On Friday 8 November 2024, the Famine Review Committee (FRC), which reviews findings of the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), issued an alert saying there was a strong likelihood that famine was imminent in areas of northern Gaza. It said famine thresholds may have already been crossed or would be in the near future, and called for immediate action from the parties to the conflict and those with influence over them.

The IPC defines famine as at least 20 percent of people facing extreme food shortages, at least 30 percent of children acutely malnourished, and two people per 10,000 dying daily. The UN humanitarian office OCHA estimated that 75,000 to 95,000 people remained in northern Gaza. World Food Programme chief Cindy McCain said the unacceptable was confirmed and that famine was likely happening or imminent in north Gaza.

UN data showed aid entering Gaza at its lowest level in a year. The United States said Israel must allow at least 350 trucks a day. COGAT, the Israeli military body, reported an October average of 57 trucks a day and 81 a day in the first week of November, while the UN put the figure at 37 daily since early October. Before the war the average was about 500 trucks a day, according to the WFP. Israel's UN ambassador Danny Danon said Hamas was hijacking aid, which Hamas denies.
